conclusion: Invoice SI-2026-0612 belongs to the year ending 30 June 2027: control passed when the customer signed delivery note DN-2026-0612 on 3 July 2026, after the 30 June 2026 year end. Revenue for the year ended 30 June 2026 is overstated by AUD 142,000.00.

reasoning_chain.text: Invoice SI-2026-0612 to Bilby Robotics Pty Ltd for $142,000 was posted on 28 June 2026.
Delivery note DN-2026-0612 was signed by the customer's representative (Daniel Price) on 3 July 2026.
Clause 5.1 of contract CON-001 (CON-001-T1): title to and risk in the goods pass to the customer when its authorised representative signs the delivery note at the delivery address.
For an obligation satisfied at a point in time, indicators of control include legal title and the significant risks and rewards of ownership (AASB 15 para 38).
Control of the goods transferred on 3 July 2026, the date the delivery note was signed.
Revenue is recognised when the customer obtains control of the goods (AASB 15 para 31).
Rule finding X-REV-08-1-R01-1 reports the same gap: posting on 28 June 2026 and signature on 3 July 2026 fall on opposite sides of the period end.

The invoice was posted on 28 June 2026 but control transferred on 3 July 2026, after the period end of 30 June 2026, so revenue of $142,000 is recorded in the wrong period and revenue for the year is overstated by $142,000. This explains rule finding X-REV-08-1-R01-1.

counter_argument: A document showing that the customer obtained control on or before 30 June 2026, such as an earlier signed delivery note or a bill-and-hold arrangement, would overturn this conclusion.
